# QC04: 敷春堂 Fuchun Tang

Wave 4 · Qichun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=QC04` · Page: `/scenes/#QC04` · Row: `research/buildings/QC04-fuchun-tang/`

## What it was

敷春堂 Fuchun Tang, "Hall of Spreading Spring", was the residence block at the centre of Qichun Yuan, on the axis from the great gate in the south-east: 迎晖殿 (勤政殿 under Jiaqing), 中和堂, 敷春堂, up to 问月楼 on the lake shore (E0524, E0572, E0567). Begun 1801 north of 迎晖殿 (E0588): a five-bay 工字 hall with 集禧堂 before it and the five-bay, two-storey 问月楼 behind; 凌虚阁 east of the rear hall, the small chapel 翠合轩, 澄光榭 south-east of 问月楼, 蔚藻堂 in a court (E0588). In 1808 Jiaqing had a south-facing gate with offices, screen wall and barriers built on the model of the Changchun Yuan gate (E0566). From 1821-22 Daoguang made Qichun Yuan the empress dowager's garden instead of repairing 畅春园, with a dividing wall from 四宜书屋 to the west wall of 正觉寺 (E0426); 敷春堂 was the dowager's residence under Daoguang and Xianfeng (E0586, E0590), housing the dowager 康慈 from 1852 (E0625). It is one of the four season halls of Jiaqing's garden, with 清夏斋, 涵秋馆 and 生冬室 (E0661). It burned on 18 October 1860 (E0680); only 18 bays of duty rooms, kitchens and a pharmacy survived (E0586).

From the inventory row: **built** 嘉庆初年 (S43); 1801; **changed** 道光元年 1821 大规模改建增饰; 戏台改盖成殿宇 (S43;S49); 同治十二年 1873 renamed 天地一家春 (never finished; S220); S224: renamed 永春堂 under Daoguang for the dowager. But S220 (1852) and an 1838 drawing title still use 敷春堂, and the 1873 edict renames 敷春堂; 1821 stage made into a hall; 1873 renamed 天地一家春 in the unfinished repair; 敷春堂 front hall: 响堂炕 (heated bed-platform) added 道光十八年正月 (1838), 地炕 in the west end bay 咸丰五年九月 (1855); the Empress Dowager 孝和 lived here 1823-1849; **destroyed** some buildings outlasted 1860; lost around 1900 (S06, S43, S49, S01, S220, S224, S361, S310).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Not in the Forty Scenes. Jiaqing's 绮春园三十景, listed in 养吉斋丛录 with Daoguang's colophon, open with 敷春堂 and include five more parts of this block: 鉴德书屋, 翠合轩, 凌虚阁, 澄光榭 and 问月楼, and 蔚藻堂 (S223 卷十八 leaf 4: 三十景者：敷春堂　鑑德書屋　翠合軒　凌虛閣 ... 澄光榭　問月樓 ... 蔚藻堂; E0448). The same text names 迎晖殿 as the main hall of the dowager's residence under Daoguang (E0448).

### How later sources differ

Dated plans: 1838 (heated beds added in the hall, 样084-7-1; E0591, E0592), 24th of the 8th month of Daoguang 30 (1850, Tsinghua PpXXI11-7: 颐寿轩, 敷春堂, east and west 所, kitchen, pharmacy; E0578, E0593), and winter 1859-60, the last before the destruction (样088-6-1; E0594, E0595). The claim that Daoguang renamed it 永春堂 (E0587) is not borne out: 1832, 1856 and 1873 documents still write 敷春堂 (E0585, E0381, E0434). In 1873 Tongzhi's project renamed it 天地一家春 and drew a new hall on its site (E0434, E0596, E0597): after the target state.

## What survives today

Service buildings stood on the site in about 2011 (E1011). Ruin photographs of a broken stone bridge are tied to it as likely (P0460-P0463). No dig found.

No excavation or survey of its remains found in this round.

## Gaps and wishlist

Four dated Yangshi Lei plans (1838, 1850, 1859-60, and the 1873 project) exist but none is viewed: the 1859-60 sheet 样088-6-1 is the best single target for the 1860 state of any Qichun compound. No sizes beyond S01.
